subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: What durable boundary should OpenClaw require before `gh-issues --cron --yes` sends untrusted GitHub issue or review text to a tool-enabled child agent?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current hardening gap, but the durable fix changes security-boundary semantics across skill prompts, subagent task construction, sandbox requirements, and possibly the public `sessions_spawn` API.

options.title: Layer runtime content wrapping with child isolation
options.body: Treat issue/review text as structured untrusted data before task construction and require sandbox or per-spawn tool narrowing for unattended workers.

options.title: Accept prompt-only guardrails
options.body: Land skill-template warnings as defense in depth, while explicitly accepting that tag/comment escape and child tool inheritance remain possible.

options.title: Defer to per-spawn tools only
options.body: Wait for the `sessions_spawn.toolsAllow` API and leave `gh-issues` content wrapping for a later separate pass.

recommendation.title: Layer runtime content wrapping with child isolation
recommendation.body: Treat issue/review text as structured untrusted data before task construction and require sandbox or per-spawn tool narrowing for unattended workers.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history on `sessions_spawn`, sandbox hardening, and current skill/spawn surfaces.
